My journey with online boards started with 4chan and I slowly made my way over to Reddit. I appreciated the 4chan community a little more but reddit was just easier to navigate for a guy who is only ever online briefly. I mostly just lurked the front page, browsed /news, /tifu (ever since Jenny went to the hotel "for kisses"), and occasionally got into dialogues on /christianity.

Over time Reddit started to feel more and more forced and artificial, but I was never involved enough to keep up with any of the politics of what was going on. I didn't even know /fatpeoplehate was a thing until a comic made its way to the front page. It was basically this, except it said, "yell at fat people" in the last frame (instead of black people). I'm not sure why, but that post triggered something that prompted me to figure out what was going on. I learned about "the Fattening" and how Reddit was basically in the middle of a civil war. I read about how they were dealing with criticism and silencing people who disagreed with them in the name of "safety" and I knew I needed to get out fast.

I don't care about shaming fat people, even though I physically train people for a living. People have reasons for being "fit" that are just as destructive and unhealthy as being fat. But correcting "fat logic" certainly has an appropriate place in society and if a person wants to shame someone for being fat because they think it will push them towards a healthier lifestyle, who am I to stand in the way of that? Even if it were just hate for the sake of hate, truly stupid ideas should be left out in the open because they demonstrate for themselves how stupid they are. You don't just try to hide it and shadow-ban people. Banning cp and other illegal content is one thing, but for making fun of the fat is another.

Initially I was concerned that you need 100 upvoats to be able to downvoat someone. My thought was that it would turn this place into a hugbox on a certain base level, and why shouldn't someone who hardly has any street credit be able to disagree? If ideas should stand on their own merit, what is so threatening about a stranger? But I suppose it does limit throwaway accounts that just shitpost and sabotage other people's content.

So here I am, sucking up to you guys so that I can one day downvote you too. Like you (I assume), all I'm looking for is a place where people can agree and disagree in peace. If this place goes hokey, I'll jump ship again too until one day I'm just anonymously attaching sticky notes to everything I see in public that I feel deserves a response. But I don't think we need to be the same or hold the same opinions to get along. Being able to disagree and still be bros is the mark of a healthy society.

So I look forward to being forced to re-evaluate my opinions from you guys and to calling you out on yours.

-Crux
